Raise length-frequency samples to the total catch

Source: R/lfqRaise.R
lfqRaise.Rd

The function raises the sampled numbers of fish per length class (`lfq$catch`) to the total catch, using the total landings in weight and the weight of the samples. This is required for methods that need absolute numbers, such as the length-based virtual population analysis (VPA). Methods that only use the relative length composition (e.g. ELEFAN, catchCurve) and the resampling (lfqResample) work with the sampled numbers.

Usage

lfqRaise(
  lfq,
  landings,
  sampleWeight = NULL,
  by = "sample",
  a = NULL,
  b = NULL,
  LW_unit = "kg"
)

Arguments

lfq

a list of the class "lfq" consisting of following parameters:

  • midLengths midpoints of the length classes,

  • dates dates of sampling times (class Date),

  • catch matrix with the sampled numbers of fish per length class (rows) and sampling date (columns),

  • par (optional) a list with the parameters of the length-weight relationship (a and b), required if sampleWeight is not provided.

landings

total landings (or catch) in kg: one value per sample (by = "sample") or per year (by = "year"). With by = "year", the values are matched to the years by their names if named, otherwise they are used in the order of the years.

sampleWeight

optional; the weight of the samples in kg (one value per sample or year, as landings). By default (sampleWeight = NULL), the weight is estimated from the sampled numbers and the length-weight relationship: sum of catch * a * midLengths^b. Use the measured weight of the samples if available.

by

"sample" (default) to raise each sample (column of lfq$catch) separately, or "year" to raise all samples of a year with one factor (landings of the year / weight of all samples of the year).

a, b

optional; parameters of the length-weight relationship (W = a * L^b). By default taken from lfq$par.

LW_unit

unit of the weight in the length-weight relationship (a): "kg" (default) or "g".

Value

The lfq list with the raised catch (numbers of fish) and the element raising, a data frame with the landings, the sample weight, whether the sample weight was estimated, and the raising factor per sample or year.

Details

The raising factor of each sample (or year) is the landings divided by the weight of the sample(s). Raising each sample separately (by = "sample") gives each sample the weight of its landings, e.g. months with large landings get more weight than months with small landings, independent of the number of fish measured.

Keep the original lfq data with the sampled numbers for all other analyses. In particular, the bootstrap functions (lfqResample, ELEFAN_GA_boot, ...) require the sampled numbers, because they resample the measured fish. Instead of raising the data beforehand, the landings can be passed directly to VPA (argument landings), which raises the data (or each resample with boot) internally.

Examples

data(synLFQ7)
## length-weight relationship (W in g)
synLFQ7$par <- list(a = 0.015, b = 3)
## landings in kg at the sampling dates (one value per sample)
landings <- seq(20000, 40000, length.out = length(synLFQ7$dates))
lfqR <- lfqRaise(synLFQ7, landings = landings, LW_unit = "g")
lfqR$raising
#>       sample landings sampleWeight estimated   factor
#> 1 2016-01-01 20000.00     14836.23      TRUE 1.348051
#> 2 2016-03-02 22857.14     15289.33      TRUE 1.494973
#> 3 2016-04-02 25714.29     15659.33      TRUE 1.642106
#> 4 2016-07-02 28571.43     15974.05      TRUE 1.788615
#> 5 2016-08-01 31428.57     16554.03      TRUE 1.898545
#> 6 2016-10-01 34285.71     14380.58      TRUE 2.384167
#> 7 2016-11-01 37142.86     14515.66      TRUE 2.558813
#> 8 2016-12-01 40000.00     14859.87      TRUE 2.691813

## one raising factor per year
lfqY <- lfqRaise(synLFQ7, landings = c("2016" = 240000), by = "year",
                 LW_unit = "g")
lfqY$raising
#>   year landings sampleWeight estimated factor
#> 1 2016   240000     122069.1      TRUE 1.9661
